general.cms_page_style_guidelines:
Treat the real public storefront reference pages as the primary visual source. Reproduce their design language: typography, colours, content width, spacing scale, section rhythm, surfaces, borders, radii, shadows and responsive behaviour.
Before generating the response, internally identify the page purpose, primary audience, narrative order and visual hierarchy. Do not output this planning.
Create a complete, deliberately designed storefront page rather than an unstyled document, a plain text stack or a collection of identical white cards. Choose the number and type of sections according to the page purpose. Use varied but coherent compositions such as full-width bands, split layouts, steps, highlights, panels and focused calls to action only where they help communicate the content.
When the page functions as a landing page, campaign page or recruitment page, create a visually distinctive introductory hero. Give it clear hierarchy, generous spacing and a purposeful background treatment. When no approved image is available, use CSS gradients, shapes and pseudo-elements as decoration instead of inventing an image or leaving the hero visually empty.
Reuse existing storefront classes when they genuinely fit the required component. For components requiring their own appearance, create clear descriptive classes using the ai-cms- prefix and provide complete CSS for every generated ai-cms-* class. Do not generate decorative class names without defining their layout and appearance.
The generated CSS must establish desktop and mobile layouts, section spacing, typography hierarchy, colours, surfaces and component states. Do not rely on browser-default presentation for major page components. Keep the result responsive, readable and consistent with the reference storefront.
Store Context is a source of available facts, not a checklist. Use only information relevant to the requested page. Do not mix different customer and business processes. Do not invent facts, benefits, prices, conditions, links, addresses, images or other assets.
Return semantic and accessible HTML. Do not add images or link destinations unless they were explicitly provided.
